data.name: Manisha
data.gender_notes: Manisha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manisha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'manas', meaning 'mind'. It symbolizes the intellect, wisdom, and understanding. In Hindu mythology, Manisha is also the name of the goddess of knowledge and learning. The name Manisha carries the meaning “Mind, Intellect” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manisha usually hope their child will grow to embody mind, intellect and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Manisha is a beautiful yet profound name in Hindu culture, representing intellect and wisdom. It is usually given to a girl child, instilling a sense of promise for a bright and knowledgeable future. The name evokes images of intelligence, learning, and academic excellence. Manisha's cultural significance extends beyond just personal achievements, as it is also associated with the pursuit of knowledge and the enrichment of one's mind.
data.spiritual_significance: Manisha holds deep spiritual significance in Hindu belief, as it embodies the essence of the goddess of knowledge and learning. The name is a constant reminder of the importance of the mind and intellect in the spiritual journey. By honoring the goddess of knowledge, the name is believed to bestow blessings of wisdom and understanding upon the person bearing it. Manisha is an inspiring name for those seeking spiritual growth, as it symbolizes the power of the mind and the importance of acquiring knowledge to uplift the soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manisha symbolizes the enlightened mind, filled with divine wisdom and eternal bliss. It signifies the pursuit of knowledge and the illumination of the inner self.

vedic_reference.note: Manisha is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Manas' (mind) and 'Isha' (lady, ruler). It symbolizes the power of the mind and one's innermost desires.

historical_references.reference: Manisha was an important Jain Tirthankara, who is believed to have lived around 500 BC in the region of what is now Rajasthan, India. She is considered to be the 24th Tirthankara of the present age, and is revered by Jains for her enlightenment and teachings.

Manisha was also the name of a famous poetess and the queen of King Bhoja of the Paramara Dynasty in central India around the 11th century AD. She composed several poems and hymns in Sanskrit, and her works are still studied and appreciated in Indian literature.
